# Codex specifics for testing

<!-- Generated by testing. The rules above (AGENTS.md) are the contract. This file only tells Codex how the harness is wired. -->

## Path-scoped rules

Detailed, stack-specific rules must be read before working on files in the matching
directories. When you are about to **create** a test file (the rule cannot load before the
file exists), read the matching rule first:

- `.codex/rules/unit-tests.md` — Node Vitest tests in `web/src/**/*.test.ts` and
  `packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts`; excludes browser tests and Playwright suites.
- `.codex/rules/fixtures.md` — test fixtures, factories and seeds; lint-rule source-code
  fixtures are input data, not runnable tests.
- `.codex/rules/component-tests.md` — `web/src/**/*.browser.test.tsx`, frontend
  models/components under `web/src`, and `packages/design-system/src`.
- `.codex/rules/e2e.md` — `e2e/**` and design-system Playwright tests; distinguishes
  application integration, UI, update and journey suites. Never edit generated
  `.features-gen` output.

<!-- testing:mode=standard -->

## Mode: standard

AGENTS.md and the path-scoped rules are the contract; the hooks enforce the hard limits
(no snapshot updates, no `--no-verify`, no config edits to fix a test, lint on test
files). Nothing else is prescribed step by step — you are trusted to know when a procedure
applies. The skills are available on demand:

`$testing:test-as-spec`, `test-plan-by-level`, `mutation-loop`, `review`,
`legacy-characterize`, `integration-boundaries`, `external-contract`, `e2e-select`,
`flaky-triage`.

Two things stay non-negotiable: run the **whole** suite before you stop, and run
`$testing:mutation-loop` on new logic tests **before the PR** (not on every save — before
the PR).

Need mutation testing and the self-review enforced on every session (a team that is only
starting, tests nobody reads before merge, a money module)? `$testing:mode strict`.

<!-- /testing:mode -->

## Hooks installed in this repo

- `PostToolUse` on test files — **blocks**: snapshots, fetch/axios mocks, `try/catch`
  without assert, `expect(fn())…toThrow` without the wrapper, loops/conditionals around
  `expect`, test-id/CSS locators and class-based visibility in component tests, fixed
  pauses in E2E, exported object fixtures. **Warns**: numbers in test names,
  `toHaveBeenCalled*`, `.only`/`.skip`, a mocked repository, chained act/assert groups,
  time without fake timers. A blocked edit comes back with the list — fix the test, do not
  fight the hook; `// testing-ignore` with a reason is the escape hatch for a deliberate
  exception.
- `PreToolUse` — **denies** in Bash: snapshot updates (`-u`, `--update`), `--no-verify`,
  force push, changing Stryker thresholds from the command line, deleting test files.
  **Denies pending explicit human approval** before editing runner/mutation config files
  (when a test fails, the fix is in the test, not in the config) and before any edit that
  adds a `// Stryker disable` comment (excluding a mutant is a human's verdict); denies
  edits to `__snapshots__`.
- `Stop`: reminds you to run the full suite (parallel, random order); in **strict** mode
  also demands mutation testing on the logic your tests cover and, once the report exists,
  a verdict on every surviving mutant (test gap / implementation boundary / equivalent) in
  your final message. At most two Stop blocks per session. These are heuristic reminders,
  not proof that commands passed.

## Commands

Run from the repository root with mise (or an already activated mise toolchain).

| Command                                        | Scope                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `mise exec -- yarn test`                       | Existing workspace Node/tooling checks; not the complete browser/business suite.                                                                              |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:coverage`              | Application Node coverage, including untested source and 100%-covered files; no browser/E2E coverage and no coverage gate.                                    |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:mutation`              | Local Stryker report for `web/src/modules/mock-paper/domain/mock-paper.ts`; no CI gate.                                                                       |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:mutation --dryRunOnly` | Validate Stryker setup without evaluating mutants.                                                                                                            |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:behavior`              | Application integration specifications.                                                                                                                       |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:browser`               | Rendered component integrations.                                                                                                                              |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:e2e`                   | Selected full-system journeys.                                                                                                                                |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:ui`                    | Browser/touch UI and release-update checks.                                                                                                                   |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:storybook`             | Design-system Storybook checks.                                                                                                                               |
| `mise exec -- yarn test:all`                   | All the suites above except coverage/mutation, sequentially at the suite level to avoid shared preview/build collisions; each retains its configured workers. |

Replay a Node seed with
`mise exec -- yarn workspace @einbuergerungstest/web run -T vitest run --sequence.seed=<seed>`;
use the seed printed by the failing run. Preserve `fileParallelism: false` in lint-rule
tests. Browser/Gherkin project order is not randomized.

Stryker uses the
[Vitest runner](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/vitest-runner/) with related
tests. The
[dry-run option](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/configuration/#dryrunonly-boolean)
validates execution, not test quality or mutation score.

## Model notes

The author and reviewer use the current model; do not set a separate `reviewerModel`. Use
`.codex/agents/test-reviewer.md` as instructions for a fresh read-only subagent when a
test review is requested. Human review remains required before merging tests. No
weak/local model workflow was requested.

Standard mode was chosen explicitly. MSW and fast-check are not installed. Do not add
dependency imports or claim their helpers exist. Mutation testing is local, scoped and
report-only; changing scope or adding a CI gate requires a separate infrastructure
decision.

## Installation and activation

`config.toml` enables the hooks feature, and `hooks.json` registers the adapter.
Installation does not establish project or exact hook trust. Review the generated commands
in Codex `/hooks`; only an actual trusted Codex session can demonstrate activation. A
shell smoke check is not proof of session enforcement.

The copied adapter consumes Codex `Bash` and `apply_patch` hook events and records its own
evidence in the temporary directory. A guard request becomes a denial because hooks cannot
ask interactively. After explicit human approval of the exact operation, run only the
one-use `approve.mjs` command printed in that denial, then retry the identical operation.
Preserve existing authorization; never self-approve.

The bundled checks are heuristic: they record command text rather than successful
completion, Stop can accept a Vitest run as full-suite evidence, and strict self-review is
an accompanying reminder rather than an independent block. The bundled Stop checker also
normalizes a configured mutation command to `npm run test:mutation`; this root npm script
delegates to Yarn, but a Yarn-only command may not be recognized in strict mode. Do not
claim these hooks prove all suites passed or enforce every review step. Hook files are
copied unchanged from testing 0.1.1; plugin maintenance is outside this setup.

## Where to start

Owner decisions: existing tests are not trusted as examples; study and the mock exam are
the priorities; no money/access priority was identified. Characterize the affected
behavior before refactoring, with expected behavior from `docs/requirements.md` and
`docs/CONTEXT.md`. Distinguish documented requirements from observed legacy behavior;
report discrepancies to the owner. Do not rewrite existing tests or implementations as
part of initialization.

| Order | Module                                                                      | Change evidence (last year, detector sample)                                      | Incidents / money or access                      | First step                                                                                                                                   |
| ----- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1     | `web/src/pages/study/study.model.ts` and `web/src/modules/question-session` | Study model 7 changes; session component 6; detector found no adjacent model test | Incidents not supplied; no money/access priority | `$testing:legacy-characterize`: one-answer feedback, navigation, session reset, and persisted progress at the existing integration boundary. |
| 2     | `web/src/modules/mock-test` and `web/src/pages/mock-test`                   | Summary component 5 changes; no module-level churn count in detector sample       | Incidents not supplied; no money/access priority | Characterize timer deadline, completion/unfinished state, editable answers and scoring against requirements.                                 |
| 3     | `web/src/modules/mock-paper`                                                | No churn count in detector sample; dedicated Node tests exist                     | Incidents not supplied; no money/access priority | Review/pin approved quotas and random-input boundaries before changing selection; initial Stryker scope is this single pure file.            |

The detector's missing-adjacent-test flag is not evidence that integration coverage is
absent. It also counts generated `.features-gen` tests. Do not infer test quality or
coverage from its count.

The initial Node baseline was 46 passing application tests in 0.475 seconds. A rough
multiplier of 30–100 estimates 14–48 seconds plus startup for mutations; it is not a
measured mutation run. Only mock-paper is initially eligible: other priority models
collaborate with browser/storage state and must not be added blindly. Any production
extraction needs the owner's approval first.

## Network boundaries

The question bank, illustrations and PWA resources are owned static assets; use the actual
resources for existing browser/integration tests. Umami is the only external service
identified and is outside the correctness path for study/exams. No neighboring-team API
contract or parallel frontend/backend development applies. Before a future external API
fake, use `$testing:external-contract` and obtain the actual contract. MSW was explicitly
deferred; adding an interceptor is a future scoped change, not permission to mock the
subject under test.

## Known debt and unrelated findings

- The mock-start behavior step must wait for `mock.pending()` to clear before the next
  step advances the fake clock. Route loading can still persist the question position
  after `startMock()` returns. On master run 39073124973 (2026-10-17), jumping 60 minutes
  fired that write's 30-second timeout before IndexedDB delivered its completion event,
  throwing `InvalidStateError` from `transaction.abort()`. An instrumented local run
  reproduced the exception with a navigation save pending. PR and master source trees were
  identical; preserve state-based synchronization, not a sleep or a longer timeout.
- Stryker 10's Vitest adapter joins nested suite names with spaces, but Vitest 5's
  test-name filter uses suite separators. In the group-migration work (2026-10-16), this
  produced apparent survivors with `testsCompleted: 0`. Flat test names, matching the
  existing mock-paper suite, restored actual mutant execution. Check executed test counts
  before interpreting a mutation report; no runner configuration was changed.
- Do not run commands that regenerate Panda styles while the behavior Vite server is
  testing. Code generation can trigger document reloads and destroy in-flight browser
  evaluations. Concurrent edits from another chat can have the same effect. Run Stryker
  separately too: its sandbox copies `tsconfig.json` files that Vite treats as reload
  triggers, and concurrent Playwright cleanup can remove files during the sandbox copy.
- On 2026-10-16, the WebKit `installed app links` review-navigation check in
  `e2e/tests/app-links.test.ts` once stayed on `/pwa/progress?tab=mock-tests` after
  clicking the completed mock's link instead of opening `/pwa/progress/tests/<id>`. It
  passed unchanged in a focused rerun with the same production build. The source of the
  intermittent failure is unconfirmed; no timeout, assertion, or retry setting was
  changed, and the test remains in the full suite.
- Existing offline unit tests stub `fetch`; the copied hook may report those lines when
  that file is edited. Resolve in the scoped test task; initialization does not migrate
  them.
- Existing browser files contain CSS lookups/iteration that may trigger heuristic lint
  findings. Do not weaken assertions or add blanket suppressions; explain intentional
  exceptions where appropriate.
- The initial run emitted Node's localStorage experimental warning; it still passed.
- PR #19 repair aligned `.github/workflows/run-check.yml` with Playwright 1.64.1. Keep the
  container tag aligned with the Playwright packages when updating dependencies; a
  mismatch prevents the shared browser-launch prerequisite from reaching any tests.
- `e2e/README.md` links to missing `docs/bdd-migration.md`. The current
  requirements/context and README define ownership for this setup.

## Assembly decisions

A-CORE, A-UNIT, A-FIXT, A-HOOKS, A-REVIEWER and A-FULLRUN install the shared harness.
B-FE, B-E2E, C-FE-1/6/7/8 and C-E2E-1 preserve React Browser Mode, Reatom, explicit
scenario locales, Storybook and Playwright. C-RUN-1/7/9 provide Vitest coverage and
shuffled Node runs. C-MUT-1 and D3 add local report-only mutation infrastructure for one
pure file. D4 records the owner-approved characterization order; C-MD-2 inherits the
current model and C-MD-4 preserves Gherkin step/check structure. B-NO-BE removes
backend/DB rules. C-DBL-4 was considered and MSW explicitly deferred. CI jobs and existing
test implementations are unchanged.

## Harness verification (2026-10-15)

- `mise exec -- yarn test`: passed 46 application tests, 443 lint-rule Vitest tests and 20
  ast-grep checks. Shuffled Node runs printed a reproducible seed.
- `mise exec -- yarn test:coverage`: passed and generated `web/coverage/index.html`;
  statement coverage was 7.65% for application Node tests only. Browser/business suites
  are outside this report, so this is not the application's total behavioral coverage.
- `mise exec -- yarn test:mutation --dryRunOnly`: passed 43 related tests and instrumented
  47 mutants in the single configured pure file. No mutants were executed and no mutation
  score is established by this check.
- Stryker 10's sandbox requires the classic TypeScript compiler API. `.yarnrc.yml` gives
  only `@stryker-mutator/core@10.0.0` the same `npm:@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2`
  dependency convention already used for tooling here. Runtime resolution confirmed
  TypeScript 7.0.2 for the application and 6.0.2 with a working
  `parseConfigFileTextToJson` for Stryker. Do not downgrade the application compiler or
  bypass sandbox processing.
- Hook CLI smoke checks passed: empty input, an accepted fixture, a rejected snapshot
  fixture, and an adapter denial for a prohibited command. All five copied hook files
  matched the installed plugin by bytes. This does not establish trust or activation
  inside a real Codex session.
- JSON, unresolved-placeholder, formatting and diff-whitespace checks passed. Existing
  application/browser tests were not rewritten. Browser, business integration and E2E
  suites were not rerun for these harness-only changes.
